Business domain map: Bunkai TMS

Generated 2026-11-13 from upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging 63d5e7e3, live staging (read-only role), the business data, API and E2E maps of the same date, and the August 2026 legacy markdown as input.

Overview

Confidence: Medium-High for what the code does, Low for strategy statements: the target repo's own vision document (.context/business/business-model.md in upex-bunkai-tms) calls itself "vision locked" and has not changed since August 2026. Positioning lines such as "the art of breaking down a kata into its applications" are marketing copy, not behaviour.

Problem statement

Most test management tools store free-form test documents with traceability as an optional add-on. Bunkai attacks that in the data model: an ATC (Acceptance Test Case) cannot exist without a User Story and at least one of its Acceptance Criteria, refused by the database with ac_outside_user_story (lib/atcs/errors.ts, data map entity-atcs). A Test is an ordered chain of ATCs, a Run snapshots that chain when it starts (data map entity-run-snapshot), and a failed step becomes a Bug that carries the run, step and ATC context.

So the chain US -> AC -> ATC -> Test -> Run -> Bug is structural, not a convention a team has to keep by discipline. One ATC edit reaches every Test that uses it (affected_test_count, ADR-0009 in the target repo).

Target users

  • Human roles enforced by the code (workspace_members.role, lib/types.ts): viewer (read only), member (authors content), admin (manages members and settings), owner (creator; billing, export, deletion). The owner role can never be granted by invite.
  • Machine callers: AI agents, CLIs and CI pipelines holding a personal access token (PAT, bk_pat_*) with scopes atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin (lib/api/capabilities.ts).
  • Segments named by the plan ladder (lib/billing/plan-tiers.ts): small free teams (Community), paying teams up to 25 seats (Cloud), contract customers (Enterprise). Personas: e2e map sections persona-owner, persona-admin, persona-member, persona-viewer, persona-agent.

Value proposition (what already ships)

  • Structural traceability from story to bug, plus traceability, coverage and metrics views over it.
  • Reusable ATCs: edit once, every Test that chains it changes.
  • Step-by-step runs with image evidence, executed by a human, an agent or CI over one shared model (runs.executor_mode).
  • Native bugs born from a failed step, with forward-only lifecycle.
  • REST API with OpenAPI docs and PATs so agents can author and execute.
  • Jira Cloud story import, test plans and milestones with a sign-off verdict, team chat, notifications and a daily email digest.
  • Plan limits and Stripe billing (Community, Cloud, Enterprise).

QA relevance

Business aspectTesting implication
Anchoring invariantA permanent negative test: an ATC without a story or with a criterion from another story is refused.
Billing is liveTest the project cap (3 / 50 / unlimited), owner-only checkout, plan change only through the signed webhook, the 14-day grace period. Never against a real Stripe price.
Effective plan vs stored planAfter grace ends the UI and limits act as Community while workspaces.plan still says cloud (e2e map BR-061).
Seat and retention limits not enforcedDo not write blocking tests for them; ask the dev team before treating them as defects.
One shared Supabase projectEvery suite writes real data next to production data: keep cleanup strict and workspace-scoped.
Executor modesAgent and CI runs arrive through Bearer-only submission routes (api map journey-run-execution).

Discovery gaps

Could not be verified from the code; each needs a person or a deeper read.

  • Real Stripe Cloud price: the UI shows a typed constant (2400 cents per seat); the charged price comes from env STRIPE_CLOUD_PRICE_ID, never read. Source of truth: the Stripe dashboard.
  • Seat and retention limits: only the project cap is enforced. Whether seat and retention enforcement is planned or dropped needs the dev team (ADR-0014 defers invite-time seat checks).
  • ATC status writers: whether anything but unrun is ever written to atcs.status was not traced through the RPCs.
  • UI labels: the app has no i18n bundle, so labels come from JSX and can differ by screen. Three drifts are confirmed: executor "Human" vs "Manual", criterion "awaiting execution" vs "Never run", pending step "Unrun". A full UI sweep was not done.
  • Settings navigation entries "Members" and "Environments" are inert (lib/settings/nav-items.ts, href: null): unfinished or intentional, unknown.
  • Self-hosting and open-source claims of the vision document have no code behind them; whether they are still a goal needs the product owner.
  • Support channels, license and legal entity: not in the repo.
  • Whether a product CLI for PAT users exists: cli/ in the target looks like the developer framework CLI; not verified.
  • The target repo's own glossary changed 6 lines since August; the change was not analysed.
